observation.visible_scene: A white Joby eVTOL aircraft (tail registration 'N542BJ', rendered as 'N542J'/'N542JJ' in the blurrier early frames) flies low over a dry, brown grass airfield with a concrete perimeter wall, hangar buildings, a line of trees and distant hazy mountains under a partly cloudy sky. The craft has six rotor pods on angled booms (two rear, two mid, two front), a dark tinted cabin canopy, and a fixed tricycle landing gear with three wheels extended. The propeller blades are continuously blurred, indicating the rotors are spinning throughout.
visible_changes: The aircraft remains roughly centered in the frame across all samples while the background (hangars on the left, tree cluster on the right, perimeter wall) steadily scrolls toward the left edge and partially exits the view, indicating the camera pans/tracks rightward and the aircraft advances forward (nose-right) relative to the ground rather than sitting still.
Rotor blade blur is present in every frame, so the propulsion system is running continuously; no start-up or shutdown of the rotors is observed within the excerpt.

Landing gear stays fully extended and the cabin canopy, tail boom and 'Joby' logo remain visible and unobstructed the whole time; the only apparent change in the registration text is a sharpening of focus/angle from an indistinct 'N542J' to a clear 'N542BJ', not a physical change.

The aircraft's attitude (slight nose-down, tail boom angled up-left) and its height above the foreground field look broadly steady; no clear climb, descent, banking or tilt-transition of the rotor booms is supported by the frames.
The clip is a single continuous shot with no visible editing cut or seam.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether this low forward pass is part of a take-off, a landing approach, or a level hover/transition maneuver, and what happens before t=0 or after t=2.67s.
The true airspeed and any change in altitude, since both ends of the segment are arbitrary crop boundaries.
Whether the occupants in the cabin are active pilots or ballast, and the flight phase (VTOL vs wing-borne).
uncertain_details: Exact vertical motion of the aircraft relative to the ground is hard to confirm; apparent altitude looks constant but the moving background makes small climbs/descents ambiguous.

The split between camera panning and aircraft translation cannot be fully separated from background cues alone, though the consistent centering of the craft plus leftward background drift favors a tracking camera following forward-moving aircraft.
Minor within-frame drift of the aircraft's horizontal position (a few pixels) is too small to attribute confidently to object motion versus camera framing.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
